summary.description: Finds communities in the reviewed graph and turns each into a circle for the scrolling narrative. It re-derives them with the same rules as the client so narration stays matched to the circles shown on screen, then orders them by the main people’s birth years.
summary.input: the reviewed graph

summary.description: Identifies the metaphors and coined terms that carry the story’s theme before translation begins. It keeps only images with a real counterpart in the target language; otherwise it records their plain meaning for consistent use across the story.
summary.input: the story’s own text

summary.description: Selects the people who belong in the theme and frames their work as a narrative with themes and eras. It uses recorded places and events alongside biographies, which lets place-based topics rest on where people worked as well as how they are described. When editors supply people, it builds the story around that set.
summary.input: the person registry

summary.description: Collects every dated life event for the selected people and orders them by time. It leaves relevance and chapter placement to later steps because the initial chapter ranges are only rough guesses.
summary.input: the selected people and life events
summary.output: a chronological list of dated events

summary.description: Judges the unfiltered event pool against the story’s theme and keeps only landmark contributions. It records why each event belongs or fails, so later chapters rest on substantive claims instead of chronology or biography.
summary.input: the unfiltered event pool

summary.description: Fits the proposed eras to the events that survived curation. It assigns every event to a chapter, including events outside the proposed ranges, then drops empty chapters and sets each remaining span from its events.
summary.input: the surviving events and chapter plan

summary.description: Places each chapter in the public events that directly changed the subjects’ lives or work. It leaves weakly connected landmarks out, so historical context supports the biography instead of becoming a general timeline.
summary.input: the fitted chapters and selected people

summary.description: Combines the selected people’s ego networks into a shared social graph. It preserves each person’s account of ties between selected people and keeps only acquaintances who connect multiple selected people, so the graph highlights bridges across their stories.
summary.input: the selected people and ego networks

summary.description: Reviews the merged social graph against the article evidence, adding missed direct ties and removing weak or indirect ones. It adjusts its threshold to the graph’s existing density before clustering turns the reviewed ties into circles.
summary.input: the deterministically merged graph

summary.description: Turns each detected circle’s ties into a short card story. It keeps the people and links factual while giving the network section a readable narrative; later composition can revise these cards, and the interface falls back to ties if this step fails.
summary.input: the detected circles and their ties
summary.output: a card story for each circle

summary.description: Groups rated events into map stops when every event in a group falls within the geographic limit. It favors clusters with more story weight and landmark events, then orders the selected stops by time so the map follows the story's chronology.
summary.input: located events and per-event weights

summary.description: Rates each located event by how much its place carries the story’s theme. The map branch uses these ratings as clustering weights, so places tied to the work rise above incidental settings.
summary.input: the historical chapters and life events

summary.description: Turns the strongest geographic clusters into short factual map-stop stories. It also removes accidental or secondary groupings, so the map follows the story’s arc instead of becoming a list of locations.
summary.input: the qualifying geographic clusters

summary.description: Composes the assembled material into one top-down story and gives each component a shared voice. It orders the sections, rewrites supporting text, and curates map stops so the page advances one argument about the connected lives.
summary.input: the circle narration, map stops, and research
summary.output: a composed story with curated map stops

summary.description: Writes the composed story as a durable story record. It leaves the story available for the landing-page registry and later publication steps.
summary.input: the composed story document

summary.description: Derives a visual language for the article from its theme and opening. It sets the dark palette, typography, background pattern, and recurring marks that carry the same geometric idea from prose separators to the closing rule. The shared motif ties the timeline, network, map, and article into one editorial surface.
summary.input: the saved story’s framing and opening
summary.output: a visual identity for the meta story

summary.description: Translates the meta story for the target language. It reuses settled image wording and person translations so event titles and names match the chapters and story slides.
summary.input: the meta story and localized person data

summary.description: Builds a depth report for each selected event from the reviewed story, related articles, and biographical material. It also replaces pooled citations with event-specific sources, accepting only URLs supplied to the call, and leaves image searches tied to details in the report.
summary.input: the reviewed events, articles, and network
summary.output: depth reports, sources, and image searches

summary.description: Turns each chapter concept into an abstract light-drawn emblem. It uses the portrait style as a rendering reference while the concept supplies the subject, which keeps chapter slides visually aligned without inventing a second factual image.
summary.input: chapter concepts, colors, life events, and style
summary.output: chapter illustrations linked to life events

summary.description: Turns each chapter’s events into an abstract opening-image concept. It reads every chapter together so the concepts use distinct metaphors and avoid depicting the subject, a real place, or a historical scene.
summary.input: the chapters and life events
summary.output: an abstract art concept per chapter

summary.description: Adds biographical context for German and European figures. It carries forward usable dates, places, work, and relationships while withholding article text when its license bars derivatives.
summary.input: the Wikipedia material

summary.description: Selects the events that carry a life’s story and orders them into its major phases. It compares events across the full record, so their weight and chapter boundaries reflect the life as a whole. It leaves later steps to find places, images, and sources.
summary.input: the articles and biographical material
summary.output: a life plan with chapters and events

summary.description: Expands each event skeleton into a sourced account of the moment, with places, participants, explanatory terms, and image searches. It grounds the account in the subject’s article, then uses event-specific material to fill gaps. Failed research leaves the event unresolved.
summary.input: an event skeleton and biographical material
summary.output: a researched event account and image searches

summary.description: Resolves each researched place to map coordinates. It uses the modern name when available, so renamed historic places can appear on the map.
summary.input: historic and modern place names

summary.description: Decides the target-language form of every person name used in a biography. It favors names from target-language sources, preserves the identity and numbering of historical figures, and leaves modern names unchanged. The resulting glossary fixes each changed form across the biography and its cross-references.
summary.input: target-language names, registry, events, and network

summary.description: Judges search results against each background report and keeps only pictures that plainly show a named part of it. It reads filenames with captions because captions often describe the upload. Code limits each search to one image, so repeated views do not crowd out other illustrations.
summary.input: the reports, searches, and life events

summary.description: Searches Commons and Openverse for the planned searches, then leaves one pool of unique image candidates. It searches event-specific names in Commons first so a shared picture keeps its link to the event that requested it.
summary.input: the planned searches and event research
summary.output: a deduplicated pool of image candidates

summary.description: Scores the returned images and removes weak candidates before matching. It penalizes commemorative images so modern plaques and graves do not displace period photographs on technical quality alone.
summary.input: every hit the queries returned

summary.description: Selects a reference portrait and assigns candidate images only when their metadata supports a direct link to an event. It leaves weak matches unassigned and rejects commemorative or generic stand-ins, so images add evidence instead of decoration.
summary.input: the ranked image candidates and event skeletons
summary.output: a portrait and event images with captions

summary.description: Plans Commons searches for a portrait and for the people, works, places, and objects that carry the life story. It avoids memorials and similar later tributes, which would replace the subject’s life with images of how others remembered it.
summary.input: the event skeletons
summary.output: searches for portraits and event subjects

summary.description: Checks the chosen portrait against the subject in the image. It rejects a mismatch while keeping an unverified pick when the call fails, so a timeout cannot remove the story's only portrait.
summary.input: the portrait pick

summary.description: Gathers the target-language article and linked names that anchor later translation. When a qualified place name has no match, it also looks up the name before the comma, while preserving the qualifier for translation.
summary.input: reviewed names, life events, and ego network

summary.description: Builds a relationship map around the subject from the life events and Wikipedia material. It keeps only named people with documented direct ties, while category summaries preserve broader institutions, conflicts, and indirect influence.
summary.input: the finished life events and Wikipedia material
summary.output: an ego network of documented personal ties

summary.description: Transforms each licensed reference portrait into the collection’s shared light-drawing style. It preserves the person’s likeness while using the story colors, so portraits read as one set.
summary.input: the licensed portrait and interface colors
summary.output: a styled portrait and updated person records

summary.description: Adds the person to the landing-page index with dates, roles, summary, and the selected portrait reference. Keeps the original creation date when an entry already exists, so later runs refresh the profile without changing when it first entered the index.
summary.input: the written dataset and life events

summary.description: Reviews the life story and social network as one reader will encounter them. It proposes corrections from the source material and flags gaps, repeated facts, and mismatched people; later logic applies only high-confidence changes automatically.
summary.input: the life events, network, and Wikipedia material
summary.output: reviewed life events and ego network

summary.description: Derives a dark interface identity from the person’s era, field, and early life events. Tests text colors against the background and regenerates the palette once when they miss the contrast floor.
summary.input: the person summary and life events

summary.description: Translates the prose, headings, and captions that describe a person and their network. It applies the name glossary and source-language evidence, then leaves protected facts untouched by merging the translated fields back into the English records.
summary.input: person records, events, network, reports, and glossary
summary.output: localized person records and supporting text

summary.description: Fetches the main article, related article candidates, and Commons image metadata for a subject. Caches them under a stable subject ID so later phases and reruns reuse the same source material.
summary.input: a subject or article URL

summary.description: Ranks linked articles by their value as biographical context. It favors people, lived events, and personal works, so later research spends its limited context on relationships and moments that can carry the life story.
summary.input: the article and outgoing link candidates

summary.description: Writes the assembled life events as the pipeline’s durable record. Downstream steps read this record instead of the in-memory payload, which fixes the story at the point where its chapters, locations, and images come together.
summary.input: the verified portrait and coordinates
